title: Operational vs financial creditor - why the distinction actually matters
p1:
Not every person or company that is owed money stands on the same side of the law.

A supplier and a bank may both be creditors, but the outcome for them can be very different when a company faces insolvency.
p2:
Many assume that all creditors get equal treatment. That is the surprising part: the law separates creditors based on the nature of their claim.

A financial creditor usually gives money as a loan or investment, while an operational creditor is someone who provides goods or services and is waiting for payment.
p3:
This difference matters because financial creditors often play a key role in deciding the future of a distressed company, including evaluating resolution plans. Operational creditors, such as suppliers or service providers, have different rights and priorities under the insolvency process.

A simple invoice dispute and a major loan default may both involve unpaid money, but they are not treated the same way.
conclusion: Did you know that a supplier owed money and a bank owed money can have very different rights during insolvency? What do you think should decide creditor priority?
